# Summary of the 2019 Scottish Manifesto

## Constitutional Position
The document advocates for Scottish independence, arguing that decisions about Scotland should be made by people living there. It proposes holding an independence referendum, seeking a legal transfer of powers to enable this. The manifesto opposes Brexit, supporting either a second EU referendum with Remain as an option, or Article 50 revocation if necessary to prevent a no-deal exit.

## Economic Policy
The manifesto calls for ending austerity and reversing budget cuts to Scotland. It proposes investment in public services, infrastructure, and digital connectivity, including superfast broadband expansion. Economic priorities include boosting productivity through sector deals, supporting Scottish businesses through city and region deals, and establishing fair work practices such as promoting the real Living Wage and opposing zero-hours contracts. Tax fairness measures include cracking down on avoidance and evasion while opposing tax cuts for wealthy individuals and corporations.

## Social Security and Welfare
The document demands abolition of the two-child benefit cap, the associated exemption clause, and the benefit freeze. It calls for halting Universal Credit, ending benefit sanctions, and opposing any pension age increases. The manifesto supports the WASPI campaign and maintaining the Triple Lock on pensions, while pressing for free TV licences for over-75s.

## Health and Public Services
NHS protection is prioritized, with calls for matching Scottish per-capita health spending across the UK and passing legislation to prevent health services being included in trade deals. The manifesto supports devolution of drug policy to establish supervised consumption facilities and tackle drug-related deaths.

## Climate and Environment
The document outlines ambitious emissions targets: net-zero carbon by 2040 and all emissions by 2045. It opposes fracking, supports renewable energy investment, and proposes creating a Net Zero Fund from oil and gas revenues. Public transport improvements include decarbonizing railways by 2035 and investing in bus infrastructure.

## Immigration
The manifesto opposes ending freedom of movement and the hostile environment policy. It calls for devolution of immigration powers to create a Scottish-specific migration system, including a proposed Scottish Visa, to address demographic and economic needs.

## Defence
The document advocates scrapping nuclear weapons and redirecting spending to public services. It supports maintaining Scottish military bases, creating a representative body for armed forces personnel, and improving support for veterans, including housing homeless ex-servicemen.

## Democratic Reform
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post voting, abolishing the upper parliamentary chamber, extending voting rights to 16-17 year-olds and EU citizens, and establishing an independent commission for election debates.
